status: Modwerk's Model:Cycles base for OS 1.13: the pinned core-mc 0.3 source and Modwerk's ev_key_leds, selected by the SHA-256 in sdk/machines/model-cycles/base-binding.json. In development.

events.name: ev_tick
events.when: the UI compose check, about 30 times a second, before stock's own check
events.handler: void f(void *ctrl); Set *((unsigned char *)ctrl + 0x20) = 1 to ask for a redraw. Not a clock: timing follows the instrument's transport.

events.name: ev_draw
events.when: after the OS has composed the 128x64 frame
events.handler: void f(void *bmp, void *ctrl); Draw over the frame with fw_fill and fw_text; y = 0 is the bottom row. Stock's outputs are kept.

events.name: ev_key
events.when: each key event, before stock's key dispatch
events.handler: int f(void *brain, void *ev); Return nonzero to take the event: no later handler and not stock sees it. ev+12 is the key id, ev+16 its flags. Declare every gesture a handler takes in the module's claims.

events.name: ev_enc
events.when: each knob turn, before stock's encoder dispatch
events.handler: int f(void *brain, void *ev); Return nonzero to take the turn: no later handler and not stock sees it. ev+12 is the knob, ev+16 the delta.

events.name: ev_boot
events.when: once at boot, after the mods' RAM image is copied, their .bss cleared and the instruction and branch caches invalidated, before the OS starts
events.handler: void f(void); Fill tables the OS reads while it starts. The OS clears its own .bss right after.

events.name: ev_key_leds
events.when: every key-LED frame, after the frame clears the LEDs and before the stock views set theirs
events.handler: void f(void *mgr); Set an LED with fw_led_set(mgr, led, state): 2 lights it, 1 turns it off; TRIG n is LED n; the first setter wins. A module whose LEDs change sets *((unsigned char *)ctrl + 0x21) = 1 in its ev_tick handler to ask for a frame.

exports.purpose: set a key LED in an ev_key_leds handler: state 2 on, 1 off; the first setter wins (Modwerk's mc/core.h)

memory.note: DMA timer 0 stays as the stock OS has it (NO_DTIM0): a mod cannot use it as a time base.
